confirmed.title: Selected level is marked by colour alone (no ring, no weight/shape change), unlike the size control
confirmed.evidence: `.level-control button` already draws `border-width: 2px; border-style: solid; border-color: var(--color-control-border)`, and `.level-control button[aria-checked='true']` changes only `border-color: var(--color-focus)` and `background-color: var(--color-given-bg)`. The level name is bold in both states. The size control gets a non-colour cue because its border goes from `transparent` to visible and it adds `font-weight: 700`. The spec's 'Level option content' says the radio ring for the checked state is drawn by a stylesheet pseudo-element, but the diff adds no `::before`/`::after`. As a result the checked level differs from the others only by colour (WCAG 1.4.1).
confirmed.suggestion: Add a non-colour cue to the checked state: the pseudo-element radio ring from review-set-11 (filled dot when aria-checked='true', dashed ring when aria-disabled), or at least a border-width/style change. Add a stylesheet test like the one that pins the aria-disabled border-style cue.
verifierNotes: Confirmed in src/ui/style.css lines 463-490. `.level-control button` has a 2px solid border and `.level-name` is bold in every state. The `[aria-checked='true']` rule changes only border-color (--color-focus) and background-color (--color-given-bg). Only the aria-disabled state gets a non-colour cue (dashed border). The size control has a non-colour cue, a border that goes from transparent to visible. So the checked level differs from the others by colour alone, which is a WCAG 1.4.1 concern. Severity minor is reasonable.

Confirmed by reading src/ui/style.css. The `.level-control button` rule (line 463) sets a 2px solid border in `--color-control-border`. contested.title: sheet.hidePopover() is called without a guard and sits before the confirmation, so a browser without the Popover API loses the confirm path
contested.evidence: In `choose()`, the entries path runs `sheet.hidePopover(); returnToSummary = true; requestAction(action);`. Where `hidePopover` is undefined (a pre-popover engine renders the `[popover]` sheet inline, so its buttons can still be clicked), the TypeError fires before `requestAction`. The size or level change then silently does nothing, and the error goes uncaught in the click handler. In the no-entries path (line 339) the change does happen, but focus is never returned. `panelIsOpen()` already guards against a missing `:popover-open`, but this call has no matching guard.
contested.suggestion: Use `sheet.hidePopover?.()` (or a small `hideSheet()` helper with try/catch, matching `panelIsOpen`) so that the confirmation and the focus return still run. Or record that the Popover API is a hard baseline requirement in the ADR.
verifierNotes: The mechanism is real at src/ui/play-page.ts lines 328, 333 and 339. `sheet.hidePopover()` is called with no guard. In the entries path (line 333) it runs before `returnToSummary = true; requestAction(action)`. In an engine without the Popover API, `hidePopover` is undefined, so it throws a TypeError. The size or level change then silently does nothing and the click handler throws uncaught. Nothing else guards it: `panelIsOpen()` only guards the `:popover-open` pseudo-class, and the ADR/tsconfig set no Popover baseline. Impact is small. Popover is baseline in current browsers. In an engine without it, `popover="auto"` markup would show the sheet inline permanently, so the page would already be degraded. I confirm the mechanism and downgrade the severity.

The code matches the finding. In `choose()` (src/ui/play-page.ts lines 333-335), `sheet.hidePopover()` runs before `requestAction(action)`, and nothing guards it. In an engine with no Popover API, `hidePopover` is undefined, so that line would throw a TypeError and the confirmation would never open. I could not show that this happens for a real user, for three reasons. First, the whole page is built on the Popover API: the sheet and the rules panel both use `popover="auto"` and `popovertarget` (lines 44, 53, 74, 75, 87, 101). The sheet's `toggle` listener, the `:popover-open` check and `popovertargetaction="hide"` also depend on it. Without the API the summary button cannot open the sheet, the close buttons do nothing and the `toggle`-driven focus return never fires. So the failure is one symptom of an already unsupported baseline, not a separate bug. Second, the same unguarded `hidePopover()` appears at lines 328 and 339, so guarding only line 333 would not make the page work in such a browser. Third, native Popover support has shipped in Chrome 114, Safari 17 and Firefox 125. The finding is itself marked low confidence and minor, and it names no reachable user or attacker. The most it supports is a note that the Popover API is a hard requirement. I found no ADR that records this, but that is a documentation gap, not a reproducible defect.

contested.title: Light-dismiss toggle handler moves focus to the summary even when the user clicked another control outside the sheet
contested.evidence: The `toggle` listener calls `summaryButton.focus()` on every `newState === 'closed'` unless the dialog or the rules panel is open. A light dismiss caused by pressing a board cell, «Підказка» or «Нова головоломка» closes the popover on pointerdown and queues the toggle task. Focus can then land on the summary instead of the control the user pressed, so focus is split from the activated element. The spec mandates this handler and says the light dismiss is checked only in a real browser, so this should be verified in the 4.9 browser check rather than assumed.
contested.suggestion: In the real-browser check (task 4.9), confirm where focus ends after a light dismiss by clicking a cell. If focus is stolen, skip the refocus when `document.activeElement` is already a focusable element outside the sheet (other than body), and amend the spec to match.
verifierNotes: I read the toggle handler at play-page.ts ~343. It does call summaryButton.focus() on every 'closed' state unless the confirm dialog or rules panel is open, so the code matches the description. The claimed defect is that focus is stolen from a control the user pressed after a light dismiss. I could not confirm that, for three reasons. First, it depends on the ordering of the browser's mousedown focus, the pointerup light dismiss and the queued toggle task. I could not run that in a real browser here. Second, the finding itself says the outcome is unverified ("Focus can then land...", "should be verified in the 4.9 browser check"). Third, the finding says the spec mandates this handler, so returning focus to the summary after a dismiss is deliberate behaviour, not an accidental mistake. The click handlers on cells and buttons still fire whatever the focus is, so the user's action is not lost. No functional bug is demonstrated, only a possible focus-placement quirk, so I refute the finding for lack of a positively confirmed wrong mechanism.

The code at src/ui/play-page.ts lines 343-347 matches the finding. The `toggle` listener on `sheet` calls `summaryButton.focus()` for every `newState === 'closed'`. Its only guards are the confirm dialog being open and the rules panel being open. It does not check `document.activeElement`, and it does not check why the popover closed. `choose()` and the dialog handlers already refocus the summary themselves, so this listener matters mainly for Escape and light dismiss. A light dismiss from clicking a board cell, the hint button or the new-puzzle button fits the sequence below. I did not run it in a browser, so the order of events is reasoned from the HTML popover spec. The mousedown moves focus to the pressed control. The popover then light-dismisses and queues the async `toggle` event, which fires after that focus move. The handler then moves focus to the summary, away from the control the user pressed. The impact is minor: keyboard and screen-reader focus ends up on the summary instead of the pressed control. The suggested fix is reasonable, but it needs the spec amended as well. I rate the finding as confirmed by code reading, minor severity, and not browser-verified.

rejected.title: Return-to-summary focus logic is repeated in three dialog handlers
rejected.evidence: `yesButton`, `noButton` and the dialog `close` listener each read and reset `returnToSummary` and call `summaryButton.focus()` (lines 303-323). The Yes handler needs to focus after `action?.()`, so some duplication is justified. The No handler, however, could rely on the `close` listener, which already covers Escape. Three hand-maintained copies of one state flag make it easy for a later change to leave it stuck at true.
rejected.suggestion: Put it in one helper, e.g. `endConfirmation(focusSummary: boolean)`, called from the three sites, or let the `close` listener own the focus return for both Cancel and Escape.
verifierNotes:
The code at lines 301-323 matches the description. The Yes, No and `close` handlers each read and reset `returnToSummary` and focus `summaryButton`. But the finding names no wrong behavior, so it is not a correctness defect.

I traced each path:
- **Yes:** it captures `pending` and the flag, clears both, closes the dialog, runs the action, then focuses the summary. When the `close` event fires later, `returnToSummary` is already false, so there is no double focus and no stuck flag.
- **No:** it captures and clears the flag, closes the dialog and focuses the summary. The later `close` event sees false and does nothing.
- **Escape:** the browser closes the dialog, and the `close` listener clears `pending`, resets the flag and focuses the summary.
- **Flag set:** only `choose()` sets `returnToSummary = true`. It does so just before `requestAction`, which opens the dialog, so every path that opens the dialog ends in one of the three handlers above.

The "easy to leave stuck at true" claim is speculation about future changes, not a present bug. The suggestion to let `close` own the focus return is a refactor, and it could even change the timing: the `close` event fires asynchronously, while the explicit focus calls are synchronous. I could not confirm any incorrect behavior, so this is at most a minor maintainability or duplication note.

I read play-page.ts lines 255-347 and grepped every use of `returnToSummary`. The code at lines 301-323 matches the finding's description. But the finding names no input or state that makes the flag stick at true or misdirect focus, and I could not find one. The only place the flag is set is `choose()`, line 334. It sets the flag only after `hasEntries()` returns true. In that case `requestAction` always sets `pending` and opens the modal dialog (line 272), unless it is already open. The dialog can only end through Yes, No, or Escape, and each of those resets the flag. The Yes and No handlers clear it before `dialog.close()`, so the later async `close` event sees false and does not focus twice. Escape reaches only the `close` listener, which clears it. A modal dialog blocks the sheet, so `choose` cannot run again while a confirmation is open. No real-user bug occurs. The finding itself describes only a future-maintenance risk, with no way to reproduce it. That is a style or refactoring comment, not a correctness defect, and the duplication is partly justified, as the finding admits.

A centred-panel media query and a `.visually-hidden` utility are therefore expected layout. The design already uses the visually hidden prefix span. The omitted `.setup-summary`, `.setup-cue` and `.level-reason` rules are cosmetic differences from the design reference. None of them breaks a requirement. The finding's own text concedes the backdrop rule is "legal under the spec". The only remedy it offers is a documentation note. It has no wrong mechanism, no failing behaviour and no spec violation.

The CSS does exist (`.setup-sheet::backdrop` with `opacity: 0.3` at style.css:433-435, plus `.visually-hidden` at 387). But the finding itself says the rules are legal under the spec, and no user or attacker can hit any failure from it. The spec only forbids `opacity` on the four colour rules. The new backdrop opacity matches the existing `.rules::backdrop` (0.3) and `.confirm::backdrop` (0.45) patterns. The spec also says explicitly that button look and sheet layout fall under the held NFR-12/14, and it names the visually hidden prefix span. What remains is a request to add a documentation note in design.md, which is not a reproducible defect.

rejected.title: Light dismiss of the sheet and the toggle-driven focus are only stub-tested; real-browser behaviour is unverified until task 4.9
rejected.evidence: Spec «Escape, the close button and a closing toggle event change nothing» (spec.md:138): "the light dismiss ... is not claimed here and is checked in the real browser". The toggle listener (play-page.ts:343-347) moves focus to the summary on every `closed` toggle unless the dialog or the rules panel is open. In a real browser, a light-dismiss click that lands on a page control (for example a cell) will change that cell and then pull focus to the summary when the async toggle arrives. That matches the spec text, but no test checks it and it may surprise players. The panelIsOpen check depends on `:popover-open` or on focus being inside the rules panel. jsdom only reaches the second through the test's own focus call.
rejected.suggestion: Add this case to the task 4.9 real-browser check: open the sheet and click a cell outside it, then confirm the cell and focus behave acceptably. If they do not, amend the spec to limit the focus return to closes that the page or the sheet's own controls start.
verifierNotes: The code at play-page.ts:343-347 does what the finding describes: on a `closed` toggle it returns focus to the summary unless the dialog or rules panel is open. That is the documented design. The spec scenario "Escape, the close button and a closing toggle event" requires focus on the summary after a closing toggle. The spec also states that light dismiss is native to popover="auto", is not claimed by the jsdom tests, and is checked in the real browser. The suggested addition is already in task 4.9(d): "Open it, click outside: same result." Task 4.9(b) to (l) also covers the focus behaviour in a real browser. No incorrect mechanism is shown. The finding only says the case is not unit-tested and "may surprise players", which is speculation. The cell-click-then-focus-pull scenario is unconfirmed. In browsers, popover="auto" light dismiss closes the popover on a click outside it, and the focus return is the intended outcome. This is a process observation that the task list already covers, not a defect in the code.

The finding describes no defect that a user or attacker can trigger. The listener at play-page.ts:343-347 does what the spec says: it returns focus to the summary on a closed toggle, unless the dialog or the rules panel is open. The finding itself concedes that it "matches the spec text". The spec (spec.md:138) says the light dismiss is native to popover="auto" and is checked in the real browser, not in jsdom. Task 4.9(d) in tasks.md already schedules that real-browser check ("Open it, click outside: same result"). The only gap is the narrower case of a click that lands on a cell. A cell click that dismisses a popover and then moves focus to the summary is standard, accessible behaviour for a modal-like sheet. It is a speculative UX preference, not a reproducible bug, and the planned check is still pending, not missing.
